time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
units: pixels (x right, y down, full 2560x1440 resolution) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the sea-floor strip between frames: shifts < 0.3 px, random (caustic animation only); static objects keep identical positions in all frames
camera.notes: underwater scene; animated light caustics on the floor and an animated water surface at the top change pixel values but do not move the camera

perspective.water_surface_band: rows 0 to about 290 show the water surface from below
perspective.comment: 2D video: the creature moves horizontally in a plane facing the camera, at constant image row. The sea floor recedes to its far edge at y ~775, so floor objects at different image heights are at slightly different depths; the creature, its shadow and the kelp/rock are all treated as at the same plane for a single scale

creature.description: jellyfish-like creature: a translucent white/blue mesh bell (lens/half-dome shape, pink dots on its surface) seen side-on, a green core ball on the bell's left (trailing) side, and three tentacles trailing to the right: an upper tentacle curving up into a pale-green hook, a straight horizontal tentacle at y ~762 ending in two pale blobs, and a lower tentacle curving down to a pale-green hook (its middle part is barely visible against the floor). The creature moves to the RIGHT; the tentacles point right, i.e. they lead and the bell (with the core ball at its left side) trails.
creature.visible_frames: 0-71 (all); tentacle tips leave the right image edge from frame ~66 (straight tentacle) and ~71 (upper hook)
creature.reference_point: centre of the green core ball (ref_x, ref_y), the best origin proxy: it moves on a straight horizontal line (y 758.8 +- 0.9 px) while the bell outline pulses; the shadow below it moves with the same x

motion_summary_px.linear_fit_x_vs_frame: x = 573.7 + 20.968*frame (frames 1-71), rms residual 1.25 px; quadratic term 0.0009 px/frame^2 (negligible)

size_px.core_ball_diameter: about 50-60 px (matched-disk radius 29-31 px; partly hidden behind the mesh on its right side)
size_px.bell_height: pulses: about 280 px (frame 12, top 617 bottom 895) to about 390 px (frame 45, top 563 bottom 955); see bell_height_px_eye
size_px.bell_width_horizontal: bell_width_px column (bell_left_x to bell_right_x); about 170 px for frames 6-30, rising to ~200-225 px for frames 40-60 (includes a faint trailing mesh on the left)
size_px.whole_creature_length: bell left edge to straight-tentacle tip: about 600-700 px (whole_length_px column), e.g. frame 24: 1051 to 1603
size_px.whole_creature_height: upper hook top (~515-530) to lower hook bottom (~990-1018): about 470-500 px

creature_shadow.description: small dark elongated shadow on the sea floor directly below the core ball (y ~1036-1058, ~50 px long, ~6 px tall)
creature_shadow.visible_frames: 0-29, 33-71 (lost over the rock shadow region frames 30-32)
creature_shadow.notes: its x matches the core x within ~2 px (fit 20.97 px/frame), independent confirmation of the core motion

kelp_flowers.description: short kelp with purple flowers, left of the coral

coral_fan.description: black branching coral in front of the rock's left end

kelp_thin_mid.description: thin kelp at the rock's left top

rock.description: large porous blue coral rock (arched, with a dark cave under it), centre of the floor

sea_floor.description: sandy floor with moving caustics; far edge at y ~775

water_surface.description: rippled surface seen from below at the top of the frame (rows 0-290)

events.event: start of clip; frames 0 and 1 are virtually identical (mean abs diff 0.14 vs 2.3 for later pairs): creature does not move between frame 0 and 1
creature starts moving right at full speed (~21 px/frame from frame 1->2 on; no visible acceleration phase)
bell passes in front of the coral fan and rock (no contact; creature is in front, not occluded)
bell pulsation extremes: smallest (height ~280 px) near frame 12, largest (~390 px) near frame 45; bell top y: 591 (f0) -> 629 (f22) -> 563 (f45) -> 610 (f71)
straight-tentacle tip reaches the right image edge
end of clip; creature still moving right at constant speed, core at x 2063

files.tracks/creature.csv: main per-frame track (reference point, bell edges, tentacle tips, shadow, whole box)
files.tracks/bell_bottom_profile.csv: automatic bell-bottom estimates (unreliable, biased high; superseded by eye readings)
